comment: Inputs to the Review Tier classifier (ADR 0070). `rules` are ordered and first match wins; a file no rule matches takes the `tier:*` tag of the Nx project that owns it, and a file neither matches falls to `human`. The human rules come first on purpose: a broad prose rule further down must never reach a path listed above it. Lowering a path's tier means editing this file, and this file is itself a human path (item 3). Thresholds and the reach exclusions were set from the replay in docs/research/2026-09-06-review-tier-replay.md, not guessed.

rules.reason: CI workflows decide which gates run and CODEOWNERS decides who must approve; a change here changes what every later Pull Request is held to (ADR 0070 item 4).

A dependency change always moves the lockfile: CI installs with --immutable, so a package.json that pulls something new without a yarn.lock change cannot merge. The lockfile is the only record of what was actually installed.

The Assertion Gates, the hook that runs them, the config they read, and this map are the things that decide what merges; the map protects itself (ADR 0070 item 3). project.json is here because tier:* tags are the classifier's primary signal.

The reviewer's own instructions, the sub-agents that judge code, and the report contract. A Pull Request that edits how it will be reviewed is one component grading its own authority. Other sub-agents are agent-instructions.
The sandcastle loop dispatches agents with a token and merges slices into integration branches; a change here changes what runs unattended.
Root build, lint, and TypeScript configuration applies to every project at once and its failure mode is a rule that silently stops applying.
Prisma schema and migrations: a wrong migration is unrecoverable once it runs against production data.
Authentication, guards, and request middleware: the backend app is tier:human already, and these paths are listed so the human set reads in one place.
The published security policy and its supporting documents are the repo's promise to reporters; CODEOWNERS already names them.

package.json without a lockfile change is scripts and metadata, not a dependency change (see dependency-lockfiles). Forty-one of the last two hundred Pull Requests touched it without touching yarn.lock, almost always to add an npm script.
Harness instructions, skills, and the domain glossary shape what agents do next; a reviewer should read them, and a human decides only when the diff also reaches a human path.
ADRs record decisions and House Explainer Pages carry gated facts; both deserve a reading, neither can break a build.
Editor, formatter, ignore, and local-service configuration: low blast radius, but a wrong ignore pattern hides files from every later gate.
Markdown that is not an instruction file or a decision: feature docs, research, READMEs, licences. Nothing executes it.

reach.comment: Files that count toward their project's own tier but never seed the dependency walk: a story, a test, or a note cannot change what a dependent project runs.

size.comment: Lines are additions plus deletions across the diff. A diff over the `agent` ceiling is human regardless of what it touches; over the `auto` ceiling it is at least agent.

blastRadius.comment: Projects reached: the changed projects plus every project that depends on one of them, transitively, through the Nx graph.

authors.comment: Logins whose Pull Requests may classify below human. Bots (any login ending in [bot]) and every other login are human.
